details.label: Road and weather recording

name: Housekeeping Camp
summary: Seasonal riverside lodging in numbered units with concrete walls, a canvas roof, patio, bear locker and fire ring. The operator counts 266 units; the NPS building labels used for pins are not a booking inventory.
hours: 2026 season · April 3–October 12; confirm operation before travel

phones.label: Yosemite Hospitality switchboard · ask for this service

notice: Search Places for a unit number, for example 'Housekeeping site 179'. Unit pins are approximate building centres; the front desk confirms where your unit is.

details.label: The unit
details.text: Three concrete walls, a canvas roof, a privacy curtain and a covered patio. A standard unit sleeps up to six with a double bed, twin bunks and two optional cots. There are lights and outlets but no phone or TV.

details.label: Arriving
details.text: Check-in is at 4 pm and check-out at 11 am. Bring bedding or rent it on site. The desk is staffed around the clock during the season.

details.label: Services and access
details.text: Non-guests may use the laundry for a fee. The showers are only for registered guests; Curry Village sells public showers. Shuttle stop 12 is the camp's stop.

details.label: Food and fire
details.text: Everything with a scent, including coolers, toiletries and rubbish, goes in a closed, latched bear locker. Every unit has a grill and fire ring; wood fires are allowed only 5 to 10 pm and any current restrictions apply.

details.label: House rules
details.text: Quiet hours run 10 pm to 6 am. No pets other than service animals. Sleeping in vehicles or outside the units is not allowed.

details.label: Accessible units
details.text: Ask for an accessible unit when booking. The operator describes nearby parking, paved paths and accessible toilets, but the accessibility of any particular numbered unit has not been checked.

name: Yosemite Falls
summary: Among the tallest waterfalls on Earth, in three parts: Upper Yosemite Fall, the middle cascades and Lower Yosemite Fall. NPS warns it is often a trickle or dry by August.
hours: Normal season · about Nov–Jul, peak May

sources.label: NPS · current conditions (updated Oct 23, checked Oct 25, 2026)

sourceNote: NPS waterfall guide (updated May 12, 2026), rechecked October 5, 2026. Pin: NPS public GIS point 21401 (source GNIS), feature edited January 9, 2026; positional accuracy unknown. Normal season only; no current flow observation.

waterfall.normalSeason: Roughly November through July, peaking in May. Expect thundering runoff from April to June and an ice cone at the foot of the upper fall in winter.
waterfall.height: 2,425 ft / 740 m in total: upper fall 1,430 ft, middle cascades 675 ft, lower fall 320 ft
waterfall.viewing: Visible from much of the Valley, especially around Yosemite Village and the Lodge. A one-mile loop reaches the base of the lower fall, and its east side from the shuttle stop to the base is wheelchair accessible. A strenuous all-day trail climbs to the top.

name: Horsetail Fall
summary: A slender winter fall on the east flank of El Capitan. On rare clear evenings in February it can light up orange at sunset, if water is flowing.
hours: Normal season · about Dec–Apr (ephemeral)

sources.label: NPS · current conditions (updated Oct 23, checked Oct 25, 2026)

sourceNote: NPS waterfall guide (updated May 12, 2026), rechecked October 5, 2026. Pin: NPS public GIS point 21371 (source Imagery), feature edited January 9, 2026; positional accuracy unknown. Normal season only; no current flow observation.

waterfall.normalSeason: Roughly December through April. NPS says it usually runs only in winter and is easy to overlook.
waterfall.viewing: Best seen from just east of El Capitan. NPS suggests the El Capitan Picnic Area on Northside Drive west of the Lodge, or the turnouts just east of it; the fall is visible from the road. Viewing restrictions may apply in mid to late February, so check that year's NPS Horsetail Fall page rather than assuming past rules.

links.label: Yosemite Falls Parking
links.note: February 2026 only (NPS Horsetail page, updated January 14, 2026): with parking and stopping prohibited between Lower Yosemite Fall and El Capitan Crossover, NPS said to park here and walk 1.5 miles each way to the viewing area near El Capitan Picnic Area, and that Yosemite Falls parking and shuttle stop were the closest. Check that year’s rules.

summary: A thundering fall in Hetch Hetchy Valley that, as NPS notes, relatively few people make the trip to see.
hours: Normal season · all year, peak May

sourceNote: NPS waterfall guide (updated May 12, 2026), rechecked October 5, 2026. Pin: NPS public GIS point 20158 (source GNIS), feature edited January 9, 2026; positional accuracy unknown. Normal season only; no current flow observation.

details.label: Footbridges
details.text: An NPS safety project (PEPC 87715, cleared November 2019) describes five footbridges in front of the fall. In spring runoff and heavy rain the westernmost can flood and become impassable; hikers were swept off the bridges in 2011 and 2017. Whether the planned reroute was built, and the bridges' current state, are not tracked here.

waterfall.viewing: Visible from the O'Shaughnessy Dam parking lot. An uneven trail gets close to the base: NPS Hetch Hetchy hikes list five miles round trip with 507 feet of gain and loss, crossing the dam and passing through the tunnel, with views of Tueeulala and Wapama Falls.

links.label: NPS Hetch Hetchy day hikes

name: Chilnualna Falls

hours: Normal season · all year, peak May
notice: NPS conditions updated October 23 and checked October 25, 2026 say the trail to the top of Chilnualna Falls has reopened. The separate closed area east of Wawona Road, south of Glacier Point Road and north of Wawona still reaches east to the Bridalveil Creek trailhead, south of the Ostrander Lake trail, as drawn on the NPS public information map. That says nothing about other routes; check conditions before hiking.

details.label: Your unit
details.text: Three concrete walls, a canvas roof, privacy curtain and covered patio. Standard units have a double bed and twin bunks; two extra cots allow up to six guests. Lights and outlets are provided; there is no in-unit phone or TV.

details.label: Arrival & bedding
details.text: Check-in 4 pm; check-out 11 am. Bring bedding or rent it at camp. The front desk is staffed 24 hours during the operating season.

details.label: Services & access

notice: Mapped inventory, not booking availability. Current unit use and pin accuracy are not field-verified.

details.label: Your unit
details.text: Three concrete walls, a canvas roof, privacy curtain and covered patio. Standard units have a double bed and twin bunks; two extra cots allow up to six guests. Lights and outlets are provided; there is no in-unit phone or TV.

details.label: Arrival & bedding
details.text: Check-in 4 pm; check-out 11 am. Bring bedding or rent it at camp. The front desk is staffed 24 hours during the operating season.

details.label: Services & access
details.text: Laundry is available to non-guests for a fee. Showers are for registered guests only; Curry Village has public showers for a fee. Shuttle stop 12 serves the camp.

details.label: Food & fire
details.text: Keep food, coolers, toiletries and trash in closed, latched bear lockers. Each unit has a grill and fire ring; wood fires are limited to 5–10 pm and remain subject to current restrictions.

details.label: Stay rules
details.text: Quiet hours 10 pm–6 am. Pets are prohibited except service animals. Sleeping in vehicles or outside units is prohibited.

details.label: Accessible units
details.text: Request an accessible unit when booking. The operator describes nearby parking, paved paths and accessible toilets; accessibility of a particular numbered unit has not been verified.

hours: 2026 season · April 3–October 12; confirm operation before travel

phones.label: Yosemite Hospitality switchboard · ask for Housekeeping Camp

notice: Mapped inventory, not booking availability. Current unit use and pin accuracy are not field-verified.
sourceNote: NPS building inventory fetched September 21, 2026; operator property map reviewed October 1, 2026. Map and GIS numbering disagree in places: the operator lists 266 units while GIS carries 279 labels.

details.label: Your unit
details.text: Three concrete walls, a canvas roof, privacy curtain and covered patio. Standard units have a double bed and twin bunks; two extra cots allow up to six guests. Lights and outlets are provided; there is no in-unit phone or TV.

details.label: Arrival & bedding
details.text: Check-in 4 pm; check-out 11 am. Bring bedding or rent it at camp. The front desk is staffed 24 hours during the operating season.

details.label: Services & access
details.text: Laundry is available to non-guests for a fee. Showers are for registered guests only; Curry Village has public showers for a fee. Shuttle stop 12 serves the camp.

details.label: Food & fire
details.text: Keep food, coolers, toiletries and trash in closed, latched bear lockers. Each unit has a grill and fire ring; wood fires are limited to 5–10 pm and remain subject to current restrictions.

details.label: Stay rules
details.text: Quiet hours 10 pm–6 am. Pets are prohibited except service animals. Sleeping in vehicles or outside units is prohibited.

details.label: Accessible units
details.text: Request an accessible unit when booking. The operator describes nearby parking, paved paths and accessible toilets; accessibility of a particular numbered unit has not been verified.

details.label: Your unit

details.text: Keep food, coolers, toiletries and trash in closed, latched bear lockers. Each unit has a grill and fire ring; wood fires are limited to 5–10 pm and remain subject to current restrictions.

details.label: Stay rules
details.text: Quiet hours 10 pm–6 am. Pets are prohibited except service animals. Sleeping in vehicles or outside units is prohibited.

details.label: Accessible units
details.text: Request an accessible unit when booking. The operator describes nearby parking, paved paths and accessible toilets; accessibility of a particular numbered unit has not been verified.

name: Bridalveil Fall Trail
summary: A short paved walk to the foot of Bridalveil Fall. The gentle route ends at a wheelchair-accessible viewing area; a steeper path gets closer to the spray.
hours: Easy · 0.5 mi round trip, 80 ft gain
Start: Bridalveil Fall parking area or Southside Drive
accessibility: The gentle path has a wheelchair-accessible viewing area.
notice: Stay behind the barriers: the rocks at the base are wet and treacherous.

name: Lower Yosemite Fall Trail
summary: A short paved loop to the base of Yosemite Falls, the tallest waterfall in North America. The east side of the loop is wheelchair accessible.
hours: Easy · 1 mi loop, 50 ft gain
Start: Shuttle stop 6 (Lower Yosemite Fall)
accessibility: The east side of the loop is wheelchair accessible.
notice: Yosemite Falls is usually dry from late summer into autumn.

name: Cook’s Meadow Loop
summary: An easy flat loop on pavement and boardwalk with views of Yosemite Falls, Half Dome and the Merced. Wildlife is most active early and around dusk.
hours: Easy · 1 mi loop
Start: Shuttle stop 6 (Lower Yosemite Fall)
accessibility: Level pavement and boardwalk throughout.
notice: NPS describes the loop starting at the former Valley Visitor Center at shuttle stop 5 (today the Yosemite Exploration Center area, not the newer Welcome Center at stop 2) and says it can also begin at stop 6. The route traced here starts at stop 6 and keeps the Sentinel Bridge out-and-back; see the route note for how that compares with the published mile.

name: Mirror Lake
summary: Follow the paved road from shuttle stop 17 to the small lake, which reflects Half Dome in spring, then take the unpaved trail around it for the loop.
hours: Easy to moderate · 2 mi round trip, 100 ft gain / 5 mi loop, 200 ft gain
Start: Shuttle stop 17 (Mirror Lake)
accessibility: The road to the lake is paved, and placard holders may drive it.
notice: The lake is usually dry in summer and autumn.

name: Yosemite Valley Loop Trail
summary: A quiet circuit of the western Valley floor on mostly level but mixed trail, away from the crowds. Walk a short stretch or make a day of the whole loop.
hours: Moderate · 7.2 mi loop / 11.5 mi loop
Start: Lower Yosemite Fall, shuttle stop 6, for both loops; the NPS route heads west along the bike path to the Valley Loop Trail signs
notice: NPS Valley Loop Trail page (updated September 14, checked October 27, 2026): the trail over El Capitan Bridge, which links the north and south halves of the loop, is closed on weekdays through December 2026 for bridge work, with limited access on weekends. This is a dated reference notice, not live status; check conditions and signed detours before committing to a loop.

sources.label: NPS · Current conditions (updated Oct 21, checked Oct 22, 2026)
NPS · Valley Loop Trail (updated Sep 14, checked Oct 24, 2026)

name: Vernal Fall Footbridge
summary: The short but very steep opening stretch of the John Muir Trail to the footbridge and its view of Vernal Fall. Come back the same way.
hours: Moderate · 1.6 mi round trip, 380 ft gain
Start: Happy Isles, shuttle stop 16
notice: Guide 51.8 shows trail repairs with a signed detour in the Vernal Fall corridor. The work zone is open on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, and on weekdays only before 7 am and after 3:30 pm, through the end of October as conditions allow. Follow the detour signs.

name: Top of Vernal Fall (Mist Trail)
summary: Beyond the footbridge, climb the Mist Trail's steep granite stairway to the top of Vernal Fall. Spring brings heavy spray and slick steps; the John Muir Trail offers a drier way down.
hours: Moderate to strenuous · 2.4 mi round trip, 1,000 ft gain / 3.7 mi loop, 1,500 ft gain
Start: Happy Isles, shuttle stop 16
notice: Guide 51.8 shows trail repairs with a signed detour in the Vernal Fall corridor. The work zone is open on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, and on weekdays only before 7 am and after 3:30 pm, through the end of October as conditions allow. Follow the detour signs.

name: Top of Nevada Fall
summary: From the top of Vernal Fall, keep climbing the Mist Trail to the top of Nevada Fall at 5,907 feet. Return the same way or descend the John Muir Trail as a loop.
hours: Strenuous · 5 mi round trip, 2,000 ft gain / 5.8 mi loop, 2,000 ft gain
Start: Happy Isles, shuttle stop 16
notice: Guide 51.8 shows trail repairs with a signed detour in the Vernal Fall corridor. The work zone is open on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, and on weekdays only before 7 am and after 3:30 pm, through the end of October as conditions allow. Follow the detour signs.

sources.label: NPS · Vernal and Nevada Fall trails (updated Jul 27, checked Oct 24, 2026)

name: Yosemite Falls Trail
summary: A very steep, rough trail of dozens of switchbacks. The first mile reaches Columbia Rock at 5,040 feet for wide Valley views; the full route tops out above Yosemite Falls.
hours: Strenuous · 2 mi round trip, 1,000 ft gain / 7.2 mi round trip, 2,700 ft gain
Start: Camp 4, shuttle stop 7
notice: Bring sun protection, salty snacks and at least three quarts of water per person.

name: Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point
summary: A very steep climb with sweeping Valley views that ends at Glacier Point. Until early October the Glacier Point tour bus can drop hikers at the top, with no pickup.
hours: Strenuous · 4.8 mi one way, 3,200 ft gain / 9.6 mi round trip, 3,200 ft gain
Start: Shuttle stop 11 (Four Mile Trailhead)
notice: Signed Four Mile Trail parking on Southside Drive is very limited. Consider the Sentinel Beach or Swinging Bridge lots before the trailhead, or ride the Valleywide shuttle to stop 11. Obey posted restrictions and allow walking time; nearby distances are straight-line, not checked routes. Never park in the shuttle stop.

sources.label: NPS · accessibility guide (Sentinel Beach and Swinging Bridge parking)

name: Snow Creek Trail
summary: An unrelenting stack of switchbacks out of Tenaya Canyon beyond Mirror Lake, with views of Half Dome and Clouds Rest.
hours: Strenuous · 9.4 mi round trip, 2,700 ft gain
Start: Mirror Lake Trailhead, shuttle stop 17
notice: There is no drinking water on the trail or at the trailhead; carry what you need.

sources.label: NPS · Snow Creek Trail (updated Mar 11, 2024; checked Oct 23, 2026)

name: Half Dome Trail
summary: The classic all-day ascent past Vernal and Nevada Falls to the cables on Half Dome at 8,836 feet. A permit is required every day the cables are up, roughly late May to early October.
hours: Strenuous · 14 mi round trip, 4,800 ft gain / 16.4 mi round trip, 4,800 ft gain
Start: Happy Isles, shuttle stop 16
notice: Permits come from a preseason lottery (March 1 to 31) and a daily lottery; see go.nps.gov/HDpermits.
